mainTopic: מעילה on the red heifer's ashes, funding communal sin-offerings, and the חביתין after the כהן גדול dies
overview: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא saying that by Torah law there is no מעילה on the ashes of the פרה אדומה. רב אשי explains that the חכמים first added מעילה because people disrespected the ashes, then removed it when people stopped sprinkling in doubtful cases. Next, רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון argue over whether the פר העלם דבר של ציבור and the שעירי עבודה זרה are paid for by a new collection or from the תרומת הלשכה. A ברייתא from רבה זוטי shows that רבי שמעון is the one who says they come from the תרומת הלשכה. The גמרא then returns to the משנה. רבי יוחנן asks whether, after the כהן גדול dies, the חביתין is brought as a full portion in the afternoon too or is cancelled. רבא's proof from the eighth כהן is rejected by רבי ירמיה, and רבא then brings a proof from a פסוק. A ברייתא settles it: a full portion in the morning and a full portion in the afternoon. Finally, אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן argue over how much לבונה goes with the חביתין, and רבי יוחנן begins a new question about a כהן גדול who died, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: no מעילה on the heifer's ashes
steps.stepSummary: The quoted ברייתא ends by saying that one who benefits from the ashes of the פרה אדומה has not committed מעילה. This shows that the no-מעילה rule is Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: With its ashes, one is not liable for misuse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting just before this. The last line says there is no מעילה on the ashes, and that line is being used as a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא treats the rule as plain Torah law: the heifer itself carries מעילה, but its ashes do not. This seems to clash with the earlier claim that the rule about the ashes came from a תקנה of the חכמים, so an answer is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, the sin of using הקדש (holy property) for personal benefit
Its ashes, meaning the burned remains of the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: With its ashes, one is not liable for misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶפְרָהּ אֵין מוֹעֲלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a ברייתא quoted before this section, used as a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier claim that the rule about the ashes came from a תקנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא presents 'no מעילה on the ashes' as straightforward Torah law, not as a rabbinic enactment.

steps.title: רב אשי: the first תקנה added מעילה to the ashes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says there were two תקנות. By Torah law the heifer carries מעילה and its ashes do not. Because people disrespected the ashes and used them on their wounds, the חכמים decreed מעילה on the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There were two ordinances. By Torah law, one is liable for misuse with the heifer, but not with its ashes. Once the Sages saw that people were treating it disrespectfully and using it on their wounds, they decreed misuse on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by agreeing that the ברייתא states the Torah law. He then explains that the חכמים later changed the practice, and this was the first change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides end up correct: the Torah law is no מעילה on the ashes, and there also was a תקנה. The first תקנה was stricter than Torah law. It added מעילה to stop people from treating holy ashes like ordinary medicine.

keyTerms.meaning: Rabbinic enactments that adjust practice
By Torah law, as opposed to a rabbinic rule
Treating something with disrespect
They decreed, meaning the חכמים made a protective rule
The sin of personally benefiting from הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the ברייתא is wrong. The ברייתא gives the Torah law, and the תקנות are rabbinic changes added on top of it.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
There were two ordinances.
By Torah law, with it one is liable for misuse,
but with its ashes one is not liable for misuse.
Once they saw that people were treating it disrespectfully,
and were making it into salves for their wounds,
they decreed misuse upon it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: שְׁתֵּי תַּקָּנוֹת הֲוַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Historical layering: Torah law plus later rabbinic enactments
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's Torah law seemed to rule out any תקנה about the ashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא states the Torah law, and the חכמים first added מעילה as a protective decree.

steps.title: The second תקנה returned to Torah law
steps.stepSummary: When people began holding back from sprinkling in doubtful cases, the חכמים cancelled their decree and went back to the Torah law of no מעילה on the ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once they saw that people were refraining from sprinkling in cases of doubt, they set it back to Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his answer with the second תקנה, which cancelled the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict decree backfired. People worried about committing מעילה on the ashes, so they avoided sprinkling anyone whose טומאה was only a doubt. To make sure that doubtful people would still be sprinkled and become טהור, the חכמים restored the original Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Refraining or holding back
Doubtful cases of sprinkling, where it is unclear whether the person needs it
They established it, meaning they set the law back

steps.whatToRemember: By Torah law, the heifer has מעילה and its ashes do not. The חכמים first added מעילה to the ashes and later removed it, so in the end the Torah law stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the חכמים weighing one concern against another. Protecting respect for the ashes mattered less than making sure people actually got sprinkled and became טהור.

phrases.english: Once they saw that people were refraining
from sprinkling in cases of doubt,
they set it back on Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דַּחֲזוֹ דְּקָא פָּרְשִׁי מִסְּפֵק הַזָּאוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's answer with the second תקנה, which reverses the first.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the end the halacha follows Torah law: there is no מעילה on the ashes.

steps.title: How the special communal sin-offerings are funded
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: according to רבי יהודה, a fresh collection is made for the פר העלם דבר של ציבור and the שעירי עבודה זרה. According to רבי שמעון, they are paid for from the תרומת הלשכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: For the bull for an unwitting communal sin and the goats for idol worship, a new collection is made from the start for them. This is the statement of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: They come from the collection of the chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a ברייתא with a similar מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about where the money for certain קרבנות comes from. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most communal קרבנות are paid for from the תרומת הלשכה, the fund built from the yearly half-shekel. רבי יהודה says these special sin-offerings need their own new collection. רבי שמעון says they come from the regular fund, like other communal offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: The bull brought when the בית דין mistakenly permitted a כרת sin and most of the people acted on that ruling
The goats brought for the same kind of mistaken communal ruling about idol worship
Collecting money
The Temple's main fund, taken from the half-shekel collection and used for communal offerings

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The bull for an unwitting communal sin
and the goats for idol worship:
from the start, a collection is made for them,
This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:
They come from the collection of the chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new ברייתא with a parallel מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a new collection is made for these offerings. רבי שמעון: they are funded from the תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: Another ברייתא reports the opposite opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that switches the opinions of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, and asks which of the two versions is the later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא the opposite way! Which of the two is the later version?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 4. Another ברייתא has the two opinions reversed, so the גמרא asks which version is the later, reliable one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4, רבי יהודה said there is a new collection and רבי שמעון said the money comes from the תרומת הלשכה. The other ברייתא says the reverse, with רבי שמעון holding a new collection and רבי יהודה holding the תרומת הלשכה. Since the two versions clash, we need to know which one came later, because the later version is the one we rely on.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposite, meaning the opinions are reversed
The later one, the final version we rely on
Which of them?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught the opposite?
phrases.notes: Another ברייתא swaps the names: there, רבי שמעון holds a new collection and רבי יהודה holds the תרומת הלשכה.

phrases.english: Which of them is the later one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא אִיפְּכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא in Step 4 with a ברייתא that reverses its attributions.
steps.kashyaTarget: Which opinion belongs to which תנא in the ברייתא of Step 4
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second ברייתא reverses the opinions, so we cannot be sure who holds what until we know which version is later.

steps.title: The חכמים say the first version is the later one
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים suggest to רב אשי that the first ברייתא is the later one, because רבי שמעון is known to worry about negligence.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים said in front of רב אשי: Let us say the first ברייתא is the later one, because we have heard that רבי שמעון worries about negligence.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer the question from Step 5. They say the first version is the later one, where רבי שמעון takes the money from the תרומת הלשכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Elsewhere we learned that רבי שמעון worries people will be negligent and fail to pay. So it makes sense that here too he would not rely on a new collection that people might not give to. He would take the money from the fund that is already collected, the תרומת הלשכה, which matches the first version.

keyTerms.meaning: Negligence, people failing to do what they should
Is concerned, worries about a possibility
The first one

phrases.english: The Sages said it before רב אשי:
Let us say the first is the later one,
phrases.notes: The first means the ברייתא from Step 4, where רבי שמעון takes the money from the תרומת הלשכה.

phrases.english: for we have heard about רבי שמעון
that he is concerned about negligence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי: לֵימָא קַמַּיְיתָא אַחְרִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the question of which ברייתא is later.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברייתא is the later, reliable version
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first one, because רבי שמעון's known worry about negligence fits taking the money from the תרומת הלשכה.

steps.title: רב אשי says the second version could also be the later one
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof. רבי שמעון only worries about negligence when the payers get no כפרה from the offering. Here the offerings bring them כפרה, so he would not worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to them: You can even say the second ברייתא is the later one. רבי שמעון worries about negligence only for something that brings the people no atonement. For something that does bring them atonement, he does not worry about negligence.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי knocks down the חכמים' proof. רבי שמעון's worry about negligence does not apply here, so either version could be the later one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier worry was about the griddle-cake offering of a כהן גדול who died. That offering brings his heirs no כפרה, so they might not bother to pay. The פר העלם דבר and the שעירי עבודה זרה bring כפרה to the people themselves, so they will gladly give to a new collection. That means רבי שמעון could well hold a new collection, as the second version says.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. Used to show the other option still works
The latter one, the second ברייתא mentioned
Atonement brought by the offering

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's worry about negligence is limited. People are careless only about paying for something that brings them no כפרה.

phrases.english: רב אשי said to them:
You may even say the latter is the later one,
phrases.notes: The latter means the reversed ברייתא from Step 5, where רבי שמעון holds a new collection.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא חָיֵישׁ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לִפְשִׁיעָה –
phrases.english: when רבי שמעון is concerned about negligence,
that is for a matter that has no atonement in it for them,
but for a matter that has atonement in it for them,
רבי שמעון is not concerned about negligence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בָּתְרָיְיתָא אַחְרִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered by the חכמים in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that the first ברייתא must be the later one
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes רבי שמעון's worry about negligence applies everywhere. In fact it applies only where the payers get no כפרה.

steps.title: So what is the final conclusion?
steps.stepSummary: Since the debate ended without a decision, the גמרא asks what the final conclusion is about which ברייתא is later.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final word, since רב אשי's answer left the question open. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After רב אשי's דחיה, either ברייתא could be the later one. The גמרא now asks how the matter was settled in the end.

keyTerms.meaning: What was the conclusion about it? Asked when a debate has been left open

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a final decision after רב אשי left the question open.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברייתא is finally accepted as the later, reliable version

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון says the chamber funds pay
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטי brings a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון learns from the פסוק of the daily offering that the פר העלם דבר של ציבור and the שעירי עבודה זרה come from the תרומת הלשכה. This settles which version of the dispute is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטי said to רב אשי: Come and hear a ברייתא. The פסוק says, 'My offering, My food for My fire-offerings, a pleasing aroma to Me, you shall guard to offer to Me in its time.' It comes to include the bull for a communal mistaken ruling and the goats for idol worship, teaching that they are paid from the chamber collection. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה זוטי answers the open question from the last step by bringing a ברייתא where רבי שמעון clearly says these offerings come from the תרומת הלשכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two ברייתות disagreed about who says 'from the chamber funds.' This ברייתא puts that opinion in רבי שמעון's mouth, and it learns it from a פסוק. So the first ברייתא, where רבי שמעון holds this view, is the reliable version.

keyTerms.meaning: To include: the פסוק adds more cases to its rule
In its set time

steps.whatToRemember: Conclusion: רבי שמעון holds that the פר העלם דבר של ציבור and the שעירי עבודה זרה are paid from the תרומת הלשכה, as in the first ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה זוּטֵי לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabba Zuti said to Rav Ashi:
Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"My offering, My food for My fire-offerings,
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:2. This פסוק is about the daily תמיד offering.

phrases.english: of a pleasing aroma to Me, you shall take care
to offer to Me in its set time"

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת פַּר הֶעְלֵם דָּבָר שֶׁל צִיבּוּר
phrases.english: comes to include the bull for a communal mistaken ruling
and the goats for idol worship
that they come from the chamber collection,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה זוּטֵי לְרַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 8 about which ברייתא is the correct version.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which version of the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון is correct.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון holds the offerings come from the תרומת הלשכה, which matches the first ברייתא.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: the full חביתין offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's line that after the כהן גדול dies, his חביתין is brought as a complete portion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And a complete one was offered,' and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן גדול brings half of his חביתין in the morning and half in the afternoon. The משנה says that after he dies, and until a new כהן גדול is appointed, a complete portion is brought instead. The next step asks exactly what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily flour offering of the כהן גדול, fried on a griddle
Complete, a full portion rather than a half
And so on: the rest of the quoted line

phrases.english: "And a complete one was offered," and so on.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁלֵימָה הָיְתָה קְרֵיבָה וְכוּ׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the funding discussion to a new line in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the כהן גדול dies and before a replacement is appointed, his חביתין is brought as a complete portion.

steps.title: Full portion twice a day, or only in the morning?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether the משנה means a full portion both morning and afternoon, or a full portion in the morning and no afternoon offering at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said: רבי יוחנן asked: Is it a full portion in the morning and a full portion in the afternoon? Or maybe it is a full portion in the morning, and the afternoon offering is cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks what the משנה's 'complete one' means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to read the משנה. Either each of the two daily times gets a full portion instead of a half, or the morning gets a full portion and the afternoon offering simply stops. The next steps try to answer this, and step 19 settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raised a question he was unsure about
Morning
Afternoon, the time of the afternoon תמיד
Cancelled, not brought at all
Or perhaps

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yochanan asked:
Is it a complete one in the morning
and a complete one in the afternoon,
or perhaps a complete one in the morning
and cancelled in the afternoon?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the משנה line quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the full חביתין is brought both morning and afternoon, or only in the morning with no afternoon offering.

steps.title: The eighth כהן always carries the חביתין
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the משנה that the eighth כהן carries the חביתין. If the afternoon offering could be cancelled, there would sometimes be no eighth כהן for it, so it must be brought in the afternoon too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: 'The eighth carries the חביתין.' If the afternoon offering were cancelled, then sometimes you would not find an eighth כהן carrying the חביתין! When would that happen? When the כהן גדול died and they had not yet appointed another in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer רבי יוחנן's question using a משנה that lists which כהן carries what to the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה states without exceptions that the eighth כהן carries the חביתין. If the afternoon offering stopped after the כהן גדול died, there would be afternoons with no חביתין to carry. Since the משנה does not mention any exception, רבא concludes that a full portion is brought in the afternoon too.

keyTerms.meaning: The eighth, here the eighth כהן in the order of carrying
If it were so
Sometimes
What is the case? How would that happen?

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
"The eighth carries the griddle-cakes,"
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in תמיד that lists the כהנים carrying the parts of the תמיד up to the ramp, morning and afternoon.

phrases.english: and if it were so that it is cancelled in the afternoon,

phrases.aramaic: הָא זִמְנִין דְּלָא מַשְׁכַּח לֵיהּ שְׁמִינִי בַּחֲבִיתִּים!
phrases.english: then sometimes you would not find an eighth carrying the griddle-cakes!
What is the case?
Where the High Priest died
and they did not appoint another in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁמִינִי בַּחֲבִיתִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to resolve רבי יוחנן's question from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the full חביתין is brought in the afternoon as well, not cancelled.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in תמיד that lists the eighth כהן as carrying the חביתין, with no exceptions mentioned.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה sharply rejects the proof
steps.stepSummary: When the proof was told to רבי ירמיה, he dismissed it, calling the Babylonian scholars foolish and saying their teachings are 'dark.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis said this before רבי ירמיה. He said: Foolish Babylonians! Because they live in a dark land, they say teachings that are dark.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה hears רבא's proof and rejects it strongly, saying it is mistaken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה, from ארץ ישראל, calls the proof 'dark,' meaning confused and wrong. In this line he does not yet say what is wrong with it. He only makes clear that he does not accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Foolish Babylonians
A dark place, a low-lying land
Teachings, halachic statements
That are dark, meaning mistaken or unclear

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה does not give his reason in this line. Don't assume the proof has been explained away yet. He has only announced that he rejects it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis said it before Rabbi Yirmeya;
he said: Foolish Babylonians!
Because they live in a dark land,
phrases.notes: Some versions say דיתבו and some say דיתבי. Both mean 'they live,' so the meaning doesn't change.

phrases.english: they say teachings that are dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ רַבָּנַן קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof from step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The entire proof from the eighth כהן carrying the חביתין.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated in this line. רבי ירמיה only declares the reasoning mistaken.

steps.title: The seventh and ninth כהנים can also come up empty
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה uses רבא's own logic against him. The משנה also lists a seventh כהן with the סולת and a ninth with the wine, yet those items can be brought at night or the next day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that because the משנה lists an eighth כהן, the חביתין can never be missing, then what about the seventh כהן with the flour and the ninth with the wine? Would you also say they are never missing? But the פסוק teaches that the מנחה and נסכים can be brought at night, and even the next day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה explains why he threw out רבא's proof. He shows that the same reasoning would lead to a result that is clearly false.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof was: the משנה always lists an eighth כהן with the חביתין, so the חביתין must always be there. רבי ירמיה points out that the משנה also always lists a seventh כהן with the סולת and a ninth with the wine. Yet we know from the פסוק that the מנחה and נסכים can be brought later, separately from the תמיד. So at times those כהנים would have nothing to carry, and listing a כהן does not prove the item is always present.

keyTerms.meaning: Fine flour, used for the מנחה that goes with the daily offering
'Their meal offering and their libations': the פסוק that teaches these may be brought separately from the animal
Are cancelled or left out
The next day

steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה is not saying the משנה is wrong about the seventh and ninth כהנים. He is saying the משנה describes the normal case, and the normal case is not proof that something can never be missing.

phrases.english: But then, that which it teaches:
the seventh with the fine flour,
the ninth with the wine,
would you say so too, that they are never cancelled?
But 'their meal offering and their libations' teaches: even at night,
and 'their meal offering and their libations' teaches: even the next day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּקָתָנֵי: שְׁבִיעִי בַּסֹּלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reasoning behind רבי ירמיה's dismissal in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's proof from the eighth כהן carrying the חביתין (step 12)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same משנה lists the seventh and ninth כהנים, yet their items can be delayed. So a list of כהנים cannot prove an item is never missing.

steps.title: The משנה does not deal with unusual cases
steps.stepSummary: The answer must be that the משנה does not teach 'what if' cases. The same applies to the חביתין, so רבא's proof falls away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you must say the משנה does not teach unusual 'what if' cases. So too here, it does not teach the 'what if' case of the חביתין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה finishes his rejection of רבא's proof. The משנה only describes the normal daily routine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only way to explain the seventh and ninth כהנים is that the משנה ignores rare situations. If so, the eighth כהן with the חביתין proves nothing about the rare case where the כהן גדול died and no new one was appointed yet. This knocks down only רבא's proof. רבי יוחנן's question from step 11 is answered later, by רבא's פסוק in step 17 and the ברייתא in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: It does not teach 'what if' cases: the משנה deals only with the usual situation
So too, the same applies here

steps.whatToRemember: A list in a משנה describing the normal routine cannot prove what happens in a rare situation. That is why רבא's proof from the eighth כהן fails.

phrases.english: Rather, it does not teach 'what if' cases;
so too here, it does not teach 'what if' cases.
phrases.notes: Here means the eighth כהן with the חביתין, which was רבא's proof.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, דְּאִי לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the challenge in step 14 and applies it to רבא's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבא's proof only. It does not decide רבי יוחנן's question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes the משנה's list covers every situation, but the משנה only describes the normal case.

steps.title: רבא complains about which teachings get repeated
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's rejection is brought back to רבא. He complains that people repeat the weak Babylonian teachings before the scholars of ארץ ישראל but not the strong ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought it back before רבא. He said: You repeat our weak statements in front of them, but you do not repeat our good statements in front of them?
steps.whatsHappening: The scene moves back to בבל, where רבא hears that his proof was rejected. רבא reacts to that rejection, and the discussion continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ירמיה had called the Babylonian scholars foolish because of this proof. רבא answers that this is unfair: people carry the weaker Babylonian statements to ארץ ישראל, so of course they get knocked down, while the stronger ones are never shared.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought it back, meaning they reported the discussion
Our weak or poor statements
Our good or strong statements

phrases.english: They brought it back before רבא,
He said: Our weak statements you say before them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the scholars of ארץ ישראל, like רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: but our good statements you do not say before them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהְדְּרוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports רבא's reaction to the rejection of his proof in steps 13-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא complains that only weaker Babylonian teachings are passed on to ארץ ישראל. The discussion continues beyond this point.

steps.title: רבא's strong proof from the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבא says his teaching is really one of the strong ones, because the פסוק calls the חביתין 'תמיד', which makes it like the daily תמיד offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then רבא said: This teaching is also one of our good ones. The verse says 'fine flour for a meal offering perpetually', so it is just like the meal offering of the daily offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives a much stronger proof that the חביתין must be brought in the afternoon too. He gets it straight from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the משנה about the eighth כהן failed (steps 13-15). Here רבא uses the word 'תמיד' in the פסוק to show that the חביתין follows the rules of the daily תמידין. Those are brought every morning and every afternoon no matter what, so the afternoon חביתין is never cancelled either.

keyTerms.meaning: Meal offering made of flour
The daily offerings brought every morning and afternoon

steps.whyThisMatters: This answers רבא's complaint in step 16. Here is one of the strong Babylonian teachings, built on a פסוק and not on a 'what if' reading of a משנה.

phrases.english: And Rava then said:
This too is one of our good teachings,
phrases.notes: He means: the rule that the afternoon חביתין is never cancelled is a strong teaching, even though his first proof was weak.

phrases.english: for the verse says: 'Fine flour for a meal offering perpetually,'
so here it is for you, like the meal offering of the daily offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: והֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי נָמֵי טֵיבוּתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After complaining that only weak teachings get reported, רבא gives a strong proof for the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: The חביתין is brought in the afternoon too, even after the כהן גדול died and no replacement was appointed yet.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'תמיד' in ויקרא 6:13 compares the חביתין to the daily תמידין.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the question about the חביתין was finally decided.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was decided about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the final ruling on רבי יוחנן's earlier question about the חביתין when there is no כהן גדול. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's first proof from the eighth כהן was rejected, and he then brought a proof from a פסוק. The גמרא now asks for the final ruling on רבי יוחנן's question: a full portion both morning and afternoon, or a full portion in the morning with nothing in the afternoon.

keyTerms.meaning: What was decided about it? (asking for the final ruling)

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?
phrases.notes: 'It' is רבי יוחנן's question from earlier: how is the חביתין brought when there is no כהן גדול?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all the proofs and rejections, the גמרא asks for the bottom line.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final ruling on רבי יוחנן's question: after the כהן גדול dies, is a full חביתין also brought in the afternoon, or is the afternoon offering cancelled?

steps.title: A full portion in the morning and a full portion in the afternoon
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק quotes a ברייתא: when there is no כהן גדול, a full עשרון is brought in the morning and a full עשרון in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Come and hear, for a ברייתא teaches: a full portion in the morning, and a full portion in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers the question with a ברייתא. When there is no כהן גדול, they do not split one portion in half. A whole עשרון is brought in the morning and another whole עשרון in the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן גדול brings one עשרון a day, half in the morning and half in the afternoon. The ברייתא rules that without a כהן גדול each time gets a complete עשרון. So the question is settled by a direct source.

keyTerms.meaning: Complete, here a full עשרון (tenth of an איפה) of flour
Morning
Afternoon, the time of the afternoon תמיד

steps.whatToRemember: When there is no כהן גדול, the חביתין is still brought twice a day, with a full עשרון each time.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the normal case. When a כהן גדול is serving, he brings one עשרון split into two halves. The 'full and full' rule is only for when there is no כהן גדול.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Come and hear, for it is taught in a baraita:
A full one in the morning,
phrases.notes: 'Full one' means a whole עשרון of flour. The ברייתא is talking about when the כהן גדול died and was not yet replaced.

phrases.english: and a full one in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא rules that a full עשרון is brought in the morning and another in the afternoon.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Without a כהן גדול, two full עשרונות are brought each day.

steps.title: A new dispute about the חביתין
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן disagree about the לבונה brought with the חביתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן disagree about this.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts here. רבי יוחנן tells us there is a dispute about the חביתין, and the next step spells out what it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion now moves from the flour to the לבונה (frankincense) that goes with the חביתין. This line only announces who disagrees. The details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: They disagree

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Dostai and the Rabbis disagree about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flour question is finished, so a new question about the לבונה begins.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute between אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן about the חביתין.

steps.title: Two handfuls of frankincense or one handful split in half
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says two full handfuls of לבונה, one morning and one afternoon. The רבנן say one handful split into two halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says: He sets aside two handfuls of frankincense for it, a handful in the morning and a handful in the afternoon. The רבנן say: He sets aside one handful for it, half a handful in the morning and half a handful in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: Here are the two sides of the dispute. They argue about how much לבונה the כהן גדול brings each day with his חביתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that לבונה goes with the morning part and the afternoon part. אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי gives each part its own full קומץ, so there are two a day. The רבנן split one קומץ between the two parts, the same way the flour is split.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets aside
A handful (plural: קְמָצִים)
Frankincense, brought with many meal offerings
Half a handful

steps.whatToRemember: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי: two full handfuls of לבונה a day. רבנן: one handful a day, split in half.

phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Dostai says:

phrases.aramaic: מַפְרִישׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי קְמָצִים שֶׁל לְבוֹנָה,
phrases.english: He sets aside two handfuls of frankincense for it,
a handful in the morning and a handful in the afternoon.
And the Rabbis say:
He sets aside one handful for it,
half a handful in the morning
and half a handful in the afternoon.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי אוֹמֵר: מַפְרִישׁ לָהּ שְׁנֵי קְמָצִים שֶׁל לְבוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the dispute announced in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says two full handfuls of לבונה a day. The רבנן say one handful split between morning and afternoon.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what reasoning lies behind the מחלוקת between אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי and the רבנן about the לבונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the two opinions we just heard about the לבונה. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 told us what each side holds: two full handfuls, or one handful split in two. Now the גמרא wants to know why each side holds that way. It is looking for the principle underneath each opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? The גמרא's standard way of asking for the reasoning behind a מחלוקת

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the two opinions stated in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that leads each side to its view on the amount of לבונה.

steps.title: Each side's reasoning about the handful of לבונה
steps.stepSummary: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי says we never find half a handful offered. The רבנן say we never find one עשרון needing two handfuls.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי holds: we never find half a handful being offered. The רבנן hold: we never find one עשרון of flour that needs two handfuls of לבונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by giving each side a reason, and both reasons start with 'we never find'. Each side is avoiding something that has no example anywhere else in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חביתין is one עשרון split into two halves, morning and afternoon. אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי focuses on the לבונה: since half a handful is never offered, each half gets a full handful. The רבנן focus on the flour: one עשרון never gets more than one handful, so that single handful is split.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not find. There is no example of this anywhere else, so we should not invent one here
A tenth of an איפה, the standard measure of flour for a מנחה
Handfuls, the plural of קֹמֶץ

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same kind of reasoning, 'we never find this elsewhere'. They differ only in what they refuse to invent: half a handful of לבונה, or two handfuls for one עשרון.
steps.confusionAlert: In this discussion קומץ means a handful of לבונה, not the handful of flour taken from a regular מנחה.

phrases.english: Abba Yosei ben Dostai holds:
we do not find half a handful that is offered,
And the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן עִשָּׂרוֹן דְּבָעֵי שְׁנֵי קְמָצִים.
phrases.english: we do not find a tenth that requires two handfuls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא יוֹסֵי בֶּן דּוֹסְתַּאי סָבַר: לָא אַשְׁכְּחַן חֲצִי קוֹמֶץ דְּקָרֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22 by giving each side's reasoning.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבא יוסי בן דוסתאי refuses to offer half a handful, so he requires two full handfuls. The רבנן refuse to give one עשרון two handfuls, so they split one handful.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's question: a כהן גדול died and no replacement was appointed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן begins a question about the חביתין when the כהן גדול has died and no new one has been appointed yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked: if a כהן גדול died and they did not appoint another in his place...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן begins a new question, a בעיא. Here the גמרא only describes the case; the actual question continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we discussed the regular חביתין, which the כהן גדול offers every day. Now רבי יוחנן asks about a gap: the כהן גדול has died and no one has replaced him yet. This case sets up a question about how the חביתין is brought during that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Asks a question (a בעיא), raising a case whose law is not yet clear
Appointed another in his place

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised a dilemma:
a High Priest who died
and they did not appoint another in his place,

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the dispute about the amount of לבונה and asks how it applies in the time between one כהן גדול's death and the appointment of the next.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the חביתין is offered after a כהן גדול dies and before another is appointed (the question continues in the next part of the text).
